senses.label: Debased coinage
senses.summary: Rulers reduce the silver in coins, and the coins buy less.
markers: coins lose value because they contain less silver
hazards: Debasement continued in Marcus's own reign; he would know it from the treasury side.

sources.note: Reduces the weight and silver content of the denarius.

senses.label: Imperial price controls
senses.summary: The state fixes maximum prices across the empire to stop prices rising.
markers: an empire-wide decree fixes the price of goods

senses.label: Quantity theory of money
senses.summary: General price rises follow from more money circulating, such as American silver flowing into Europe.
markers: more money in circulation raises all prices

sources.citation: Jean Bodin, Reply to Malestroit (1568); David Hume, 'Of Money' (1752)
sources.note: Prices follow the quantity of money.

senses.label: Inflation as a measured rate
senses.summary: The general rise in prices is measured as an annual rate from an official price index, and governments target it.
markers: prices rise by a measured percentage each year
governments aim at a target inflation rate

sources.citation: Official consumer price indices, from the late 1910s
